ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, the graphs of the functions $y=3x$ and $y=kx+4$ intersect at the point $P(m, 3)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $3x>kx+4$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substituting $P(m, 3)$ into $y=3x$, we have $3m=3$, from which we solve $m=1$. Thus, the coordinates of point P are $(1, 3)$, \\ 
hence for $x>1$, we have $3x>kx+4$, \\ 
meaning the solution set for the inequality $3x>kx+4$ is $\boxed{x>1}$.
